tables.title: Memory pricing / supply tightness — demand-side view (CY2026)
tables.note: What the buyers (hyperscalers / OEMs / networkers) say memory inflation is doing to capex and supply.
rows: 2026 cash-capex plan RAISED ~$20B to ~$220B — 'the HIGHER COST OF MEMORY pushing this number up from our prior estimate of about $200 billion'; existing contracts hold agreed prices, NEW deals price in current memory/HDD/SSD costs
FY2026 capex raised to $125-145B — "most of that is due to higher component costs, particularly memory pricing"
~$25B of the ~$190B CY2026 capex is higher component pricing; supply constrained at least through 2026
DRAM is the #1 supply constraint (then NAND, CPUs, HDDs); repricing "every day"; customers signing 3-5 year supply agreements
Memory + silicon shortages a 1-2 YEAR phenomenon; 52-week chip lead times; accepts gross-margin pressure to secure supply
Windows OEM channel building inventory ahead of rising memory prices; PC market expected lower as memory costs lift prices

'100-YEAR FLOOD on the memory pricing, with exponential increases' - Apple RAISED iPad/Mac prices in response; cost path Dec < Mar < Jun ('significantly more') < Sep ('even higher'), carry-in-inventory offset shrinking beyond Sep and market pricing still rising; >100% of the -120bps Mar->Jun gross-margin decline was memory. 'The DRAM market has three suppliers... we're evaluating all options.'
Forecasted advanced-silicon and memory deliveries sometimes miss, causing nonlinear factory loading; pricing environment "constructive"
Elevated DRAM costs in its own image-processing computers = ~100bps gross-margin headwind through CY2026
DRAM ASP +~90% QoQ / NAND +~80% QoQ in Q1 2026; fulfillment at record low; customers pulling 2027 demand forward; gap widens in 2027
China OEMs cutting handset builds on memory supply/price squeeze; QCOM China Android shipments 'meaningfully below' end demand; bottom ~mid-2026

Fixed-price customer contracts ONLY when component costs are locked — otherwise FLOATING-cost mechanisms pass memory/SSD/HDD inflation through to customers (no margin degradation on $75B BYOH/prepaid book)
